glosses: To try to see, to pay attention to with one’s eyes.

examples.text: They kept looking at me.
Don’t look in the closet.

glosses: To try to see, to pay attention to with one’s eyes.
As a transitive verb, often in the imperative; chiefly takes relative clause as direct object.

examples.text: Look what you did to him!

glosses: To search for, to try to find.
To face or present a view.

examples.text: The hotel looks over the valleys of the HinduKush.

1769, Benjamin Blayney (editor), King James Bible, Oxford standard text, Ezekiel, xi, 1,

glosses: To expect or anticipate.

examples.text: I look to each hour for my lover’s arrival.
1596, Edmund Spenser, The Fairie Queene, Book VI, Canto XI, 1750, The Works of Edmund Spenser, Volume 4, page 139,

glosses: To express or manifest by a look.

examples.text: Soft eyes looked love to eyes which spake again,

glosses: To make sure of, to see to.

examples.text: "Look to it yourself, father," answered Telemachus, "for they say you are the wisest counsellor in the world, and that there is no other mortal man who can compare with you.[…]

glosses: To show oneself in looking.

examples.text: Look out of the window [i.e. lean out] while I speak to you.
I have[…]more feet than shoes, or such shoes as my toes look through the overleather.

glosses: To check, to make sure (of something).

examples.text: Finding it was like to overblow, we took in our Sprit-ſail, and ſtood by to hand the Fore-ſail; but making foul Weather, we look'd the Guns were all faſt, and handed the Miſſen.

glosses: To look at; to turn the eyes toward.

examples.text: Serene, smiling, enigmatic, she faced him with no fear whatever showing in her dark eyes.[…]She put back a truant curl from her forehead where it had sought egress to the world, and looked him full in the face now,[…].

glosses: To seek; to search for.

examples.text:
c. 1552–1599, Edmund Spenser, unidentified sonnet,
Looking my love, I go from place to place,
Like a young fawn that late hath lost the hind;
And seek each where, where last I saw her face,
Whose image yet I carry fresh in mind.

glosses: To influence, overawe, or subdue by looks or presence.

examples.text: to look down opposition

glosses: To look at a pitch as a batter without swinging at it.

examples.text: The fastball caught him looking.
Clem Labine struck Mays out looking at his last at bat.
It's unusual for Mays to strike out looking. He usually takes a cut at it.

glosses: Pay attention.

examples.text: Look, I'm going to explain what to do, so you have to listen closely.

glosses: The action of looking; an attempt to see.

examples.text: Let’s have a look under the hood of the car.

examples.text: She got her mother’s looks.

glosses: local elevado de onde se pode visualizar um panorama mais amplamente
nas artes plásticas, posição onde se pode ter uma melhor visão, em termos de perspectiva, para retratar-se uma cena, paisagem, etc.
fórmula literária que expressa a situação do narrador diante da história

examples.text: Nota: neste sentido pode ser a narrativa em primeira pessoa, terceira pessoa, onisciente, etc.

glosses: opinião própria e pessoal sobre algo (situação, momento, pessoa, etc.)

examples.text: Mas, sob o meu ponto de vista feminino, que decerto não é o mais intrépido, que melhor não é deitar-se a gente ao sol, na areia luminosa, enquanto a vaga azul, coroada de espumas brancas, vem espreguiçar-se humilde aos nossos pés, vem lamber, vencida e cariciosa, a orla dos nossos vestidos, do que ter dia a dia, hora a hora, momento a momento, de disputar ao grande inimigo torvo, misterioso, sombrio, que uiva, eternamente agonizante, a sua lamentação trágica, o solo movediço e traidor sobre o qual construímos o nosso lar sagrado!...
